evals.prompt: My repo (a Chrome side-panel extension plus a Python server that runs a browser-automation agent) is getting too big for one session and Claude keeps forgetting earlier decisions. Set up specialist agents with an orchestrator.
evals.expected_output: Survey run; Crew Plan with justified agents and a considered-and-merged list; files under .claude/agents and docs/crew; CLAUDE.md block between markers; DECISIONS.md with user-stated entries locked and inferred ones proposed; routing evals written.

evals.prompt: Tiny repo: one 800-line Python CLI, a pytest suite and a GitHub Actions workflow. Can you split it into agents like the big projects do?
evals.expected_output: Small crew (about 2-3), explicitly declining to invent more; shipper gate derived from the workflow file rather than invented.

evals.prompt: I already have docs/crew set up from a few months ago. Lots of new directories since then. Are the agents still right?
evals.expected_output: Audit mode: runs check_drift.py and the survey, re-applies the three tests, checks locked decisions against code, proposes add/split/merge/retire and asks for agreement before editing.

evals.prompt: Set up a crew for this repo. Don't ask me anything, just decide and write the files.
evals.expected_output: Proceeds without waiting for answers: unanswered facts are tagged [inferred] and listed as open questions; no locked decision is invented; the target repo's own source is not modified.

evals.prompt: Set up a crew for this repo. The project is called acme, so name the agents acme-something so they're easy to tell apart.
evals.expected_output: Agent names are plain domain slugs with no project prefix (backend-api, panel-ui, data-db), not acme-backend-api; the slug is used consistently for the agent file, its name field and its knowledge file; cross-cutting roles use their fixed slugs (crew-keeper, shipper, security-review).
